note: Calibration-day digital twin: NoiseModel.from_backend_properties() on the exact live ibm_marrakesh BackendProperties at each campaign calibration timestamp (re-fetched read-only this pass via backend.properties(datetime=...), same method validated in results/cpc_revision/historical_calibration.json). qiskit-aer 0.17.2 provides from_backend_properties. LIMITATION: thermal_relaxation=False was required -- this device BackendProperties object has no 'frequency' field for any qubit (confirmed: props.qubit_property(0) has no frequency key), and NoiseModel.from_backend_properties unconditionally calls backend_properties.frequency(q) when thermal_relaxation=True, raising BackendPropertyError. So this twin includes gate_error + readout_error only, NOT T1/T2 thermal relaxation -- it is a partial noise model, not a full replication of hardware noise sources.
caveat_tier_C: Tier C runs 4-5 used a later calibration window (2026-10-08 18:32:55+05:30); this twin uses the run1-3 window (18:13:43+05:30) shared with Tier B, since 3 of 5 Tier C runs used it.
comparison_vs_generic_fakemarrakesh: results/cpc_revision/phase1d_distances.csv (tvd_hw_vs_noisy_sim column, same cells). The calibration-day twin TVD is smaller than the generic-FakeMarrakesh TVD at every one of the 15 ladder cells, most dramatically at Tier B r=2 (twin 0.0312 vs generic 0.1414) and Tier C r=1 (twin 0.0420 vs generic 0.1198) -- the calibration-specific gate/readout error model tracks hardware noticeably better than the generic snapshot, even without a thermal-relaxation term.
